extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media scholars, and readers interested in misinformation, digital media design, and media ethics
extracted.subtask_description: A magazine news feature profiling the creator of a fake-news image generator (BreakYourOwnNews.com), describing how the tool works, its design choices, uses, and the ethical and real-world consequences of easily produced fake news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watermark and timestamp as signaling devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Every 'Break Your Own News' image has both a watermark that includes the web address and a black box in the lower left corner with a timestamp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cresswell says that this design feature serves to both advertise the site and show that the 'news' is fake; the timestamp is also described elsewhere as a 'dead giveaway' that the image is not real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low barrier to creation / speed of production
rubrics_metrics.description: Using it takes mere minutes. 'There is nothing in that image you cannot recreate in a minute in Photoshop.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tool's speed and simplicity make it easy for many people to create and share fake-news images quickly, increasing the likelihood of spread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of authentic news stills and editable headlines/tickers
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can upload real television news stills and insert the phony headlines and tickers of their choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining authentic-looking visuals with customized headlines/tickers increases the realism and potential believability of generated images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence or removal of watermark affects believability and ethical choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Small news websites and individuals have asked him to allow users to pay for a version without the watermark. He hasn’t developed one because he doesn’t want to be in the position of deciding who has good intentions and who doesn’t, and he thinks people might be more inclined to believe the parodies if there are ones out there without the watermark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing identifying signals (like a watermark) makes parody images more believable; developers face ethical trade-offs over monetizing removal of such cues because it can enable deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cues do not guarantee immunity from deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the images include elements meant to tip people off that what they’re seeing is fake, it is still possible to be deceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design cues (watermarks, timestamps) reduce but do not eliminate the risk that some audiences will interpret images as real, especially in high-attention contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator responsibility and uniqueness of harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Cresswell has come to understand that he is responsible for some misinformation on the internet, but he doesn’t see his site as being a particularly abhorrent instrument. 'If you could make something that’s misleading dangerously so with this, you are more than capable of doing that on any number of tools,' he says. 'I don’t think there’s something unique about this that makes it more malicious.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating culpability, consider whether the tool uniquely enables deception versus merely lowering the technical barrier that already exists with general-purpose tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratization of editing tools increases misinformation potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Now, not everyone has access to those tools, but they’re becoming easier in many mobile apps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As editing and image-creation tools become more accessible on mobile devices, the pool of people able to produce believable fake content expands, raising systemic risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform traction and contextual amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: The site got traction with Donald Trump supporters, many of them on Reddit; Snopes notes that, amid coverage of major hurricanes, fake stories made on BreakYourOwnNews.com were widely shared on social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The social platforms and communities where images circulate (e.g., Reddit, partisan networks) and topical news cycles (e.g., hurricanes, elections) strongly influence how widely and credibly fake images spread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate alternative uses (education, marketing, parody)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers have told him that they ask their students to create headlines based on historical events to supplement homework assignments. Corporations (e.g., Denny’s UK) and comedians have used the site for promotions or jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all uses are malicious; evaluate tools by considering legitimate pedagogical, promotional, or comedic uses alongside misuse potential when making design or policy decisions.
